should_activate.prompt: I have the lite-mcp folder but I am not technical. Build me a LAN dashboard where scheduled agents claim pending work, read my instructions, report progress, and leave results for review.
Turn this editable lite-mcp binary folder into a small inventory approval app. Add the SQLite migrations, MCP tools, dashboard widgets, and a handbook for the next agent.
Doctor this lite-mcp business app: check fails after I added 0003 and the dashboard no longer starts. Explain it without asking me to debug Python.
Is lite-mcp still the right fit for this local office workflow, or has it grown into something that needs a dedicated app?
Add another business state and review action to my existing lite-mcp app, update its domain docs, and prove peer agents can still use /mcp.
Help a peer Codex on my LAN use the job tools from this lite-mcp app, and make the dashboard clear enough for a nontechnical reviewer.

should_not_activate.prompt: Build a generic FastMCP server with OAuth and deploy it to Kubernetes.
should_not_activate.reason: Generic public-service development is outside the editable lite-mcp business-app boundary.

should_not_activate.prompt: Make this standalone Streamlit chart look better and add Plotly.
should_not_activate.reason: Standalone frontend work does not involve a lite-mcp business app.

should_not_activate.prompt: Normalize this PostgreSQL schema for a multi-tenant SaaS product.
should_not_activate.reason: Database design alone and a different deployment model should not route here.

should_not_activate.prompt: Why does uv download Python instead of using my system interpreter?
should_not_activate.reason: A runtime support question alone belongs to ordinary repository diagnostics.

should_not_activate.prompt: Create an Agent Skill for our release process.
should_not_activate.reason: Skill authoring should route to the skill-creation capability.

should_not_activate.prompt: Review the changes on this branch against the issue specification.
should_not_activate.reason: Branch review should route to code review.

progressive_reads.prompt: Build the scheduled-agent job desk in my lite-mcp folder.
Doctor why this lite-mcp dashboard fails startup after a widget edit.
Can lite-mcp safely be the public customer portal for this workflow?
Create a local equipment checkout app in lite-mcp; it has no worker queue.
Review why the lite-mcp-business-app handbook chose these Job states before changing the skill.

end_to_end.prompt: In a fresh editable lite-mcp distribution, build a scheduled-agent work desk for a nontechnical owner. A peer agent claims due work, reads an immutable instruction context, records progress, submits a result, and waits for human review.
assertions: The agent identifies scheduling as external and lite-mcp as the durable LAN handoff layer.
APP_CONTEXT.md and DOMAIN_MODEL.md are created or reconciled before implementation completes.
The Job FSM, transition guards, leases, attempts, context versions, results, reviews, and events are explicit.
Applied migration history is preserved and schema changes use the next contiguous migration.
Business MCP tools are named and narrow; retriable mutations are idempotent and stale leases are rejected.
Dashboard writes use parameterized supported helpers and expose actionable errors.
The full create-to-review loop is verified through check, invoke or MCP, and the dashboard.
LAN connection instructions use the tested printed LAN address and /mcp.
The completion report states limitations and any escalation trigger.

end_to_end.prompt: Build a tiny LAN-only visitor log in lite-mcp for one receptionist. It needs data entry, a daily dashboard, and a peer agent tool for summaries, but no job queue.
assertions: The agent uses the business-first workflow without forcing the canonical Job domain onto the app.
The schema, tools, widget, and local docs use visitor-log language.
The agent still applies migration, parameterization, validation, check, startup, LAN, and escalation rules.

end_to_end.prompt: The app stopped starting after a new tool and migration. Diagnose and repair it without losing my data.
assertions: The agent starts with non-mutating inspection and check --format json.
It preserves applied migrations and user data, backs up before a necessary data repair, and fixes the reported source instead of bypassing startup validation.
It classifies retryability and verifies startup, health, dashboard, and MCP after repair.
It keeps the repair scoped to the diagnosed failure and does not enter the Develop workflow or redesign the business domain.
